scope: Independent citation-only pass based exclusively on supplied claims and primary-source retrieval; no other project files inspected.
evidence_policy: Primary paper text and publisher/author metadata; Crossref API checked for the AAAI DOI. Secondary search hits were not relied upon.
overall_verdict: Proposed literature descriptions are supportable with qualifications; add Qin et al. (ICLR 2025) and avoid broad task-level novelty.
key_corrections: Qin et al. 2025 precedes Ding et al. on no-target/one-to-many temporal retrieval.
Ding presence branch pools cross-modal embeddings, not explicit temporal coordinates.
Kim presence reads intermediate pixel-decoder features; plurality uses text features.
QD-DETR already trains on negative video-query pairs, though its original evaluation does not establish GMR rejection.
QVHighlights already supports multiple disjoint moments.
FlashVTG conference year is 2025; its preprint is 2024.
All supplied arXiv DOIs are DataCite DOIs, not Crossref registrations.
Repository module inclusion and runtime savings require implementation or experimental evidence outside this pass.
OpenVMR is ACM MM 2024 despite its arXiv upload in 2026.
Negative-aware retrieval and explicit rejection were studied before the current work by OpenVMR and Moment of Untruth.

references.title: Retrieving Any Relevant Moments: Benchmark and Models for Generalized Moment Retrieval
references.evidence_level: Primary full text and arXiv metadata
issues: Do not imply first introduction of no-target/multiple-target temporal retrieval; Qin et al. precedes this work.
Presence consumes cross-modal embeddings, not explicitly predicted temporal coordinates.
references.resolved_wording: Ding et al. study retrieval of all relevant intervals or an empty set, introduce Soccer-GMR, and attach an existence branch using max-pooling and a two-layer MLP over cross-modal localization representations.

references.title: Improving Target Presence and Plurality Recognition for Generalized Referring Image Segmentation
references.venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence 40(7)
references.evidence_level: Primary publisher full text, publisher metadata, and Crossref API
issues: Specify intermediate pixel-decoder features for presence; plurality is supervised from text-conditioned query features.
Evidence concerns image segmentation, not temporal retrieval.
references.resolved_wording: Kim, Lee, and Kwak introduce a target query that reads intermediate pixel-decoder features for presence recognition, a plurality classification objective, and synthetic no- and multi-target training examples in generalized referring image segmentation.

references.title: QVHighlights: Detecting Moments and Highlights in Videos via Natural Language Queries
references.evidence_level: Primary full text and arXiv metadata
issues: QVHighlights already includes multiple disjoint moments per query; do not characterize every earlier benchmark as strictly single-moment.
Its evaluation does not establish empty-set rejection.
references.resolved_wording: QVHighlights introduces Moment-DETR for query-conditioned moment localization and highlight detection, including retrieval of multiple disjoint moments.

references.title: Query-Dependent Video Representation for Moment Retrieval and Highlight Detection
references.evidence_level: Primary full text, arXiv metadata, and CVF proceedings
issues: QD-DETR explicitly uses irrelevant video-query pairs with low-saliency supervision; avoid saying it has no negative-query training.
Original evaluation uses retrieval/highlight metrics, not a GMR empty-set rejection protocol.
references.resolved_wording: QD-DETR builds query-dependent video representations with cross-attention and negative-pair saliency training. These evaluations do not by themselves establish no-target GMR rejection.

references.title: Correlation-Guided Query-Dependency Calibration for Video Temporal Grounding
references.evidence_level: Primary full text and arXiv metadata
issues: Latest retrieved version is v4, July 2024; 2023 denotes first preprint.
No publication venue was verified; do not invent one.
references.resolved_wording: CG-DETR calibrates cross-modal query dependence using adaptive attention with dummy tokens and clip-word correlation guidance. Its reported grounding/highlight evaluations do not establish GMR empty-set rejection.

references.title: Knowing Where to Focus: Event-aware Transformer for Video Grounding
references.evidence_level: Primary full text and arXiv metadata
issues: Evaluation uses standard grounding datasets and recall/mAP; no-target rejection cannot be inferred from these results.
references.resolved_wording: EaTR uses event-aware dynamic moment queries informed by input-specific content and position.

references.title: FlashVTG: Feature Layering and Adaptive Score Handling Network for Video Temporal Grounding
references.claim_match: Supported; publication year differs from preprint
references.evidence_level: Primary full text, arXiv metadata, and CVF proceedings
issues: Use 2025 when citing the WACV conference version; 2024 is the preprint year.
Its TFL replaces the traditional decoder; original metrics do not establish no-target rejection.
references.resolved_wording: FlashVTG uses temporal feature layering across multiple scales and adaptive score refinement for grounding and highlight detection.

references.title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
references.evidence_level: Primary full text and arXiv metadata
issues: Original language-model efficiency findings are not measurements of this repository.
No repository runtime or memory result was inspected in this independent pass.
references.resolved_wording: LoRA freezes pretrained weights and learns low-rank update matrices. Actual runtime, memory, and inference savings for this implementation require direct measurement.

references.title: CVA: Context-aware Video-text Alignment for Video Temporal Grounding
references.claim_match: Literature claim supported; repository attribution requires implementation check
references.evidence_level: Primary full text and arXiv metadata
issues: QCD selects background replacements using query relevance and preserves the ground-truth moment with adjacent context.
Whether this repository implements only the inspired replacement and excludes CBD/CTE was not inspected.
references.resolved_wording: CVA introduces Query-aware Context Diversification, motivating query-conditioned background replacement. Attribute only this augmentation inspiration unless the implementation also adopts CVA’s encoder or boundary loss.

references.title: Generalized Video Moment Retrieval
references.claim_match: Strong prior art; limits task-level novelty
issues: OpenReview direct access triggered browser verification; official ICLR PDF retrieved successfully.
Official PDF names the fifth author Shawn Li; secondary indexing may show Li Li.
No DOI was found in retrieved primary material.
No-target and one-to-many temporal retrieval, a corresponding dataset (NExT-VMR), and BCANet predate Ding et al. 2026.
references.resolved_wording: Qin et al. previously formulate Generalized Video Moment Retrieval with no-target and one-to-many queries, introduce NExT-VMR, and propose BCANet. Any present novelty must concern the specific method, benchmark, protocol, or measured behavior rather than first enabling these query types.

references.title: Moment of Untruth: Dealing with Negative Queries in Video Moment Retrieval
references.evidence_level: Primary arXiv abstract and CVF publisher abstract/metadata
issues: Negative queries mean video-irrelevant queries, not necessarily linguistic negation.
This prior limits claims that negative-query rejection itself is novel.
references.resolved_wording: Flanagan, Damen, and Wray introduce Negative-Aware Video Moment Retrieval, distinguishing in-domain and out-of-domain negatives, and evaluate retrieval and rejection on augmented QVHighlights and Charades-STA benchmarks.

references.title: Not All Inputs Are Valid: Towards Open-Set Video Moment Retrieval using Language
references.venue: Proceedings of the 32nd ACM International Conference on Multimedia
references.evidence_level: Primary arXiv abstract and publisher-deposited Crossref metadata
evidence_locations: arXiv abstract and author publication comment
issues: ACM page returned HTTP 403; Crossref confirms publisher bibliographic metadata.
Cite ACM MM 2024, not 2026, when discussing chronology.
Paper defines OOD as video-irrelevant queries; do not equate this automatically with Flanagan’s out-of-domain-negative category.
references.resolved_wording: Fang et al. study Open-Set Video Moment Retrieval and propose OpenVMR to reject video-irrelevant queries before localizing moments for relevant queries.

references.title: When One Moment Isn't Enough: Multi-Moment Retrieval with Cross-Moment Interactions
references.evidence_level: Primary arXiv abstract and author metadata
issues: The named module is Multi-moment Post-verification; generic cross-moment verification is acceptable but less precise.
Abstract supports multiple-moment retrieval, not an empty-set rejection claim.
references.resolved_wording: Cao et al. introduce QV-M² and FlashMMR for multi-moment retrieval; its Multi-moment Post-verification module adjusts boundaries, re-evaluates candidates, and prunes low-confidence proposals.
